title: Split MemoryApplicationService into retrieval, mutation, and diagnostics modules
description:
Problem: `MemorySmith.App/Services/MemoryApplicationService.cs` is now 1,168 lines and acts as the central orchestration point for memory listing, lexical/semantic/hybrid retrieval, context-pack generation, diagnostics lookup, source-link lookup, create/update/delete flows, usage increments, stats, and telemetry. The current architecture backlog owns search and service-adjacent work, but no task explicitly owns this core memory-domain hotspot.

Evidence from 2026-05-26 audit:
- Largest-file scan listed `MemorySmith.App/Services/MemoryApplicationService.cs` at 1,168 lines.
- Public methods now span `GetMemoriesAsync`, `SearchAsync`, `SearchMetadataAsync`, `LexicalSearchAsync`, `SemanticSearchAsync`, `HybridSearchAsync`, `BuildContextPackAsync`, `GetAsync`, `GetDiagnosticsAsync`, `FindBySourceAsync`, `CreateAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `DeleteAsync`, `IncrementUsageAsync`, `GetStatsAsync`, `GetActivityBucketsAsync`, and `GetTelemetryAsync`.
- Search of `Data/Tasks` found no first-class decomposition task for `MemoryApplicationService`.

Desired outcome: preserve the current memory-domain API while separating retrieval/search, mutation/audit publishing, and diagnostics/stats responsibilities into bounded collaborators or modules.

Scope:
- In scope: extraction boundaries for retrieval/query, mutation/history/audit publishing, diagnostics/source lookup, and stats/telemetry concerns.
- In scope: characterization tests and benchmark-sensitive safeguards before moving retrieval behavior.
- Out of scope: changing search ranking semantics, memory JSON schema, or store contracts beyond the minimum needed for cleaner boundaries.

Dependencies:
- Coordinate with current search/semantic backlog and `TSK-0047` complexity guardrails.

Acceptance criteria:
- `MemoryApplicationService` no longer centralizes retrieval, mutation, diagnostics, and stats concerns in one file.
- Existing memory/search/context-pack behavior remains unchanged under focused tests.
- Reviewers can inspect retrieval or mutation changes without scanning the entire memory domain file.

Validation:
- Run focused `MemoryApplicationServiceTests`, search-related tests, and any impacted benchmark-sensitive tests.
- Run `dotnet build MemorySmith.slnx -v minimal`.
- Run `./Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` after task creation/update.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created during the 2026-05-26 untracked-gap audit after confirming that the current architecture backlog does not own the monolithic `MemoryApplicationService` even though it now spans retrieval, mutation, diagnostics, and telemetry concerns.
